title: Taxi Driver
tagline: Late shift. Black coffee. Long night.
about: A lonely Vietnam vet driving a night cab grows unhinged on New York's streets.
cue: Pour the coffee when Travis sits with the other cabbies at the all-night diner.
faces: The avenue outside, after the rain.
Doors never close. Night men eat at the counter, and the urn is always on.
Sit down and eat something hot before you go back out, Killer. Twelve hours on coffee is no way to drive.
Wizard, Doughboy and Charlie T. hold the corner table. Please bus your own tray.
Light says off duty. No mohawk yet. He is coming here.
Rare slices warmed in brown gravy on thick white toast, more gravy poured over. Buttered mashed potatoes and peas.
Home fries and buttered toast, rye or white.
Cooked twice in hot oil until crisp, salted hard. White vinegar on every table.
Thick slabs of the sharp stuff, dill spears, a sleeve of crackers and hot English mustard.
From the kettle, with oyster crackers.
Then to the mirror: you talkin' to me?
Buttered white loaf layered with brandied peaches, baked in vanilla custard. Served warm.
Served warm, a slice of American on top.
Strong drip with a nip of peach brandy and brown sugar, a spoonful of soft whipped cream on top.
